dodo.accepted.caveat: Eligibility is decided by the country that issued your government ID (every director/owner for companies).

dodo.grandfathered.caveat: Only merchants already onboarded before the country was prohibited may continue (enhanced monitoring); no new sign-ups.

etsy.eligible.caveat: Countries marked * on Etsy's page accept Etsy Payments through a Payoneer Payment Account.

gplay.merchant_registration.caveat: Merchant registration is required to sell paid apps, in-app purchases or subscriptions.

lemon.bank_payouts.caveat: PayPal payouts are documented separately ('200+ countries' per PayPal's list) and are not confirmed per country here. Lemon Squeezy is migrating merchants to Stripe Managed Payments.

paddle.unsupported.caveat: Paddle states it 'works with software businesses anywhere in the world with the exception of' these countries. Software only; every seller and product is reviewed before sales are enabled.

paypal_payouts.eligible.caveat: PayPal Payouts is how many platforms (e.g. creator platforms) send earnings to PayPal accounts. A country missing here may still have PayPal accounts that can buy or send.

paypal_worldwide.markets.caveat: Listed = PayPal operates a site for this market. It does NOT say whether accounts there can receive money.

polar.payouts.caveat: Payouts run on Stripe Connect Express; individuals need Stripe Express to support the 'individual' business type in your country (check per Polar's FAQ).

upwork.restricted.caveat: Upwork: 'We support a thriving network of global freelancers in over 180 countries, but we're not available everywhere.' Also excluded: Crimea, DPR, LPR, individual nationals of Cuba, SDN-listed persons, and 'any other country or region restricted by law (this changes occasionally)'. Hand-curated from the help article (not an automated collector).

whop.payouts.caveat: Payout methods (bank, PayPal, crypto) vary by country and are shown in your Whop balance screen.

youtube_ypp.signup_areas.caveat: Availability is by the channel's country. The page also carries a 10 March 2022 note pausing new Russian AdSense/AdMob/Ad Manager accounts.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Mostly not needed: the euro has been Montenegro's sole legal tender since March 2002 (unilateral euroisation), so ordinary local accounts are already in euros (Central Bank of Montenegro). Accounts in other currencies such as USD were not researched.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The PIB (poreski identifikacioni broj). Entrepreneurs (preduzetnici) and other self-employed professionals (lawyers, notaries) get an 8-digit PIB, assigned automatically by the tax authority when they register in the Central Register of Business Entities (CRPS). For other individuals without independent activity, the PIB is the identification number issued by the interior ministry (Ministry of Finance rulebook, published in Službeni list). Foreigners who need a PIB without a business apply to the Tax Administration with a JPR form (LookupTax).

L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Separate scales for salaries (0/9/15%) and entrepreneurial income. Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income (see quoted rules). Work performed while living in Montenegro for foreign clients is generally taxable there.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT (PDV) is 21% standard, with reduced rates of 15% and 7%, and 0% for exports and international transport. Registration is mandatory when turnover exceeds EUR 30,000 in the last 12 months, within 10 days of crossing it; voluntary registration is possible below. Once registered, you cannot deregister for at least three years.

sources.title: Montenegro - Corporate - Other taxes
sources.quote: VAT registration is mandatory for entities whose turnover exceeds the EUR 30,000 threshold within the last 12-month period.

sources.title: Montenegro - Corporate - Other taxes

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
